title: Edge Connector intake + prioritization playbook for air-gapped / on-prem migrations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for customers requesting 'edge connector' style bridges (temporary or permanent) that enable limited egress for air-gapped or restricted VPC/on-prem migrations. Playbook must balance security constraints, upgrade windows, engineering runway, and business impact while producing a clear next-step for SE/PM/Eng and a documented decision record.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with SEs, Infra Eng, and Security. Collected 8 recent customer requests and 3 pilot trial notes (one closed successfully, two paused due to network topology).
2026-03-04: Draft intake form created (see links). Initial scoring weights proposed: customer_risk 30, compliance_criticality 25, upgrade_complexity 20, business_impact 15, runway_availability 10.

2026-03-07: Security review: cannot recommend any permanent outbound tunnels without HSM-backed key exchange and replay protections; suggested mitigation: ephemeral connector with strict ACLs and per-job audit logs.
2026-03-09: Eng spike (ENG-20890) estimated 6w to built a hardened connector; decision to provide an interim documented manual runbook for high-priority customers.
2026-03-11: Presented draft playbook to GTM; they requested a fast-path lane for < $100k ARR customers with sandbox-only connector approvals.
decision: Implement a two-lane intake and prioritization flow: 1) Fast-path (low-risk, sandbox-only or transient trials) with a templated ephemeral connector and expedited approval (1-2 weeks); 2) Standard lane (production, high compliance) that triggers full security and architecture review and maps to Dedicated or Private projects. Do not support permanent outbound connectors without HSM/KMS integration and signed customer acceptance of residual risk.
acceptance_criteria: A templated intake form is published and linked in the SE playbook
A prioritization rubric with numeric scoring is available and applied to new requests
Fast-path approval checklist (legal, security, SE) is published and train-the-trainer session completed
Ownerable next-step created for every open request (eng spike / pilot / decline) within 3 business days
Metrics: track 1) time-to-decision, 2) percent of requests triaged into fast-path, 3) post-decision customer satisfaction survey deployed
scoring_rubric: Scoring (0-100): customer_risk (30) = presence of regulated data / PII / PHI (0-30); compliance_criticality (25) = SOC2/ISO/PCI need (0-25); upgrade_complexity (20) = number of required infra changes / windows (0-20); business_impact (15) = ARR & go-live urgency (0-15); runway_availability (10) = SE/Eng capacity and partner availability (0-10). Fast-path threshold: score <= 35 and no regulated-data flag. Standard review: score > 35 or any 'regulated-data' true.
notes_for_eng: Eng to provide a minimal supported connector spec (ephemeral TLS + mTLS + per-job token rotation) as part of the spike. Also evaluate using existing Dedicated tunnels vs new connector service. Document rollback/incident path and monitoring signals.
